title: Longest Square Streak in an Array
summary: Given an integer array nums, find the longest subsequence where each element (after the first) is the square of the previous element, and the subsequence is sorted in ascending order.
statement: Given an integer array nums, find the longest subsequence where each element (after the first) is the square of the previous element, and the subsequence is sorted in ascending order. Return the length of this subsequence, or -1 if no such subsequence exists. A subsequence is formed by deleting some or no elements from the original array without changing the order of the remaining elements.
constraints: Choose values from nums and sort the chosen subsequence in increasing order; original positions do not constrain the sorted streak.
Each value after the first must equal the square of its predecessor.
Return the greatest streak length, or -1 when no streak has at least two values.
hints: Store all values in a set for constant-time successor checks.
From each possible start, repeatedly square while the value remains present.
Keep lengths of at least two, otherwise return -1.
Every valid streak is the deterministic chain x,x²,x⁴,... from its smallest member, so following every start finds the longest chain.

tests.explanation: Choosing 2,4,16 creates a three-value square streak.
No value’s square is present, so no length-two streak exists and the answer is -1.
